Maharashtra: IMD Issues October Heatwave Warning; Check Yellow Alert In THESE Regions
Authorities have advised residents to keep track of official weather updates and take precautions in this heat. Drink a lot of water to stay hydrated and avoid going out in the afternoon sun.
Mumbai is experiencing hot weather these days, and keeping that in mind, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has now issued a yellow alert (heatwave warning) for the city. People have been advised to take care of themselves by staying hydrated and covering up. Here are the latest weather updates.
Heatwave Warning For Mumbai & Parts Of Maharashtra
Mumbai and some parts of Maharashtra have now received their first heatwave warning after the monsoon. According to The Economic Times, IMD officials have issued yellow alerts across several districts of the state. The hot weather conditions in Mumbai escalated on October 9, and dry weather is still continuing. Raigad is also experiencing similar uncomfortable weather.
The heatwave covers areas including Palghar, Thane, Mumbai, Raigad, Ratnagiri, Sindhudurg, Kolhapur and its ghats, Satara and its ghats, Sangli and Solapur. According to Mid-Day, temperatures are expected to rise by 2-3° Celsius in the next 48 hours. However, by October 12, conditions are expected to return to normal across Maharashtra.
According to Mid-Day, authorities have advised residents to keep track of official weather updates and take precautions in this heat. Drink a lot of water to stay hydrated and avoid going out in the afternoon sun. Try to stay indoors during the hottest hours.
Wear lightweight, loose-fitting and light-coloured clothes if you need to step out of your home. Also, carry an umbrella and wear sunscreen. Avoid drinking too many dehydrating beverages, such as tea, coffee and soft drinks, which can make you feel worse in the heat.
It’s October, but Mumbai is still facing extreme heat. Thankfully, conditions are expected to improve soon. In Delhi, residents saw sunny to clear skies, while Bengaluru also witnessed cloudy skies with a chance of light rain.

IN PHOTOS: Mumbaikars brave hot and humid weather as city swelters at 36 degrees Celsius
Updated On: 09 October, 2026 10:25 PM IST | Divya Nair
Mumbaikars braved hot and humid conditions on Friday, October 9, as the India Meteorological Department issued a heatwave warning for parts of the Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR) and Maharashtra's Konkan belt. The alert remaining in force until October 12. PICS/ASHISH RAJE
01
A woman covers her face as she steps out amid hot and humid weather in Mumbai on Friday. PIC/ASHISH RAJE
02
The Regional Meteorological Centre in Mumbai said heatwave conditions were likely at isolated places in districts of South Konkan, while hot and humid weather was expected at isolated locations in North Konkan
03
The warning comes as temperatures are set to rise across parts of Maharashtra over the next few days
04
Mumbai's iconic Gateway of India wears a deserted look amid the heatwave. The IMD has forecast a gradual rise in maximum temperatures by 2-3 degrees Celsius in some parts of Maharashtra over the next 48 hours. Temperatures are expected to increase by a further 1-3 degrees Celsius thereafter
05
Maximum temperatures in parts of interior Maharashtra are likely to remain between 37 and 39 degrees Celsius on October 9 and 10, the weather department said
06
The rising temperatures could add to discomfort, particularly in areas experiencing hot and humid conditions
07
The Mumbai Metropolitan Region includes Mumbai and adjoining areas across Thane, Palghar and Raigad districts, with the urban agglomeration spread across nine municipal corporations.
